name: Coupé-Décalé
notes: Coupé-Décalé style pack (Doc 04 template, solo-first). Abidjan's club movement, born in Paris: created around 2002–2003 by DOUK SAGA (Stéphane Doukouré) and the Jet Set crew of Ivorian expats in Paris nightclubs — champagne showmanship, designer flash, and a dance built on the boucan (making a joyful scene). The name is Nouchi slang — 'couper' (to cut/hustle) and 'décaler' (to run/shift) — the diaspora hustler's story danced out loud, and the honesty this pack keeps: coupé-décalé exploded back home in Abidjan DURING CÔTE D'IVOIRE'S CIVIL-WAR YEARS, when the country chose to dance anyway; it became the sound of joy as defiance, 'la joie de vivre' as a survival strategy. Douk Saga died in 2006; his successors (DJ Arafat and a generation of atalaku-driven stars among them) carried the sound. The pack teaches the openly-shared club vocabulary: the décalé travel step, the rolling hips-and-shoulders groove, the sagacité showman arms, and the concept-drop culture where every hit names a new move — same mechanism as Afrobeats' named moves, cross-linked. The coupé-décalé drive rides in this app's Rhythm Trainer.

seasons.finale: Film yourself grooving the coupé-décalé drive through one track — shoulders rolling, face bright, presence loud.
Film the décalé travel step both directions — the run-shift that named the dance, smooth at speed.
Film the showman arms over the travel — champagne-pour flourishes, watch-flash, crowd-work to an imaginary balcony.
Learn two named concept moves from real Ivorian dancers' videos, credit the source clips, and film both.
Take coupé-décalé to a floor — an African club night, a diaspora party — and make thirty seconds of joyful scene.

attributes.name: Club-set stamina L1
attributes.test: two tracks of continuous grooving with the energy still visible in the face — coupé-décalé is a marathon of looking effortless

attributes.name: Rolling hips L1
attributes.test: 60s of smooth hip rolls layered under moving shoulders — two engines, one chassis, no conflict

nodes.name: The coupé-décalé drive & the atalaku
checkpoints: coupé-décalé rides a fast, rolling club drive — congolese-soukous DNA sped into Ivorian club heat; the pattern is in this app's Rhythm Trainer
the ATALAKU — the hype-caller shouting names, dedications, and dance commands over the track — is the music's steering wheel; when the atalaku names a move, the floor does it
listen for the travaillement (the working of the track): builds, drops, and shout-outs structure the song more than verse-chorus does

nodes.name: The sound's family tree
checkpoints: coupé-décalé's groove descends from Congolese soukous and ndombolo club culture, remixed through Abidjan's zouglou wit and Paris club polish — West and Central Africa shaking hands on the dancefloor
its concept-drop culture (every hit names a move) feeds directly into today's Afrobeats mechanism — this app's Afrobeats pack is the next branch of the same tree
trace one chain yourself: find a soukous track, a Douk Saga track, and a current Afrobeats hit and hear the baton pass

nodes.name: Douk Saga & the Jet Set — the creators
checkpoints: coupé-décalé was created around 2002–2003 by DOUK SAGA (Stéphane Doukouré) and the JET SET crew — Ivorian expats in Paris nightclubs who built a movement from champagne showmanship, designer flash, and the boucan (making a glorious scene)
the name is Nouchi slang: couper (to cut, to hustle) and décaler (to run, to shift) — the diaspora hustler's own story, danced with a wink instead of an apology
Douk Saga died in 2006; DJ Arafat and a generation of stars carried the sound — the creators are recent, named, and mourned: credit them like the contemporaries they are

nodes.name: Joy as defiance — Abidjan's answer
checkpoints: coupé-décalé exploded in Abidjan during Côte d'Ivoire's civil-war years — the country's clubs chose joy while the news chose fear, and the dance became 'la joie de vivre' as a survival strategy
hold that honestly: this is party music with a spine — celebration in hard times isn't denial, it's a decision, and Abidjan made it nightly
when you dance it, bring actual joy or wait until you can — coupé-décalé performed grim betrays its whole biography

nodes.name: The rolling groove
checkpoints: hips roll smooth and continuous under loose rolling shoulders — two layers riding the drive at once, knees soft and springy
the face is half the move: bright, amused, in on the joke — coupé-décalé's default expression is 'I know something good'
keep it rolling through a whole track without resetting; the groove is a wheel, not a rep
mistakes: grooving with a serious face (the boucan starts above the neck)
hips and shoulders fighting for the same beat (give the hips the pulse and the shoulders the subdivisions)

nodes.name: The décalé travel step
checkpoints: the run-shift that named the dance: quick shuffling travel steps that skim sideways and back, upper body cool above busy feet
shift direction on the drive's accents — the décalé reads as gliding until the cut, then it CUTS
both directions, equally smooth: the step should look like you're being moved by the music, not walking to it

nodes.name: Sagacité — the showman arms
checkpoints: the flash layer: champagne-pour flourishes, watch-taps, lapel-brushes, crowd-work waves — arms that narrate wealth and welcome over the groove
sagacité (the concept Douk Saga named) is charm as choreography: every gesture aimed at someone, even solo — pick a spot on the wall and win it over
flourishes land ON accents and dissolve between them — flash without timing is just waving

nodes.name: The concept drops — learning named moves
checkpoints: coupé-décalé runs on CONCEPT DROPS: hits arrive naming a new move (the era of guantanamo, grippé, and their hundred siblings) and the atalaku teaches the floor in real time
learn two named concepts from real Ivorian dancers' videos — note the song, the artist, and the dancer you learned from, same discipline as the Afrobeats pack
the meta-skill is fast absorption: watch, mark, try, full-out within one song — the floor won't wait for perfectionism

nodes.name: Enjaillement — the joy full-out
checkpoints: enjaillement is Nouchi for letting the joy all the way out — the freestyle state where groove, travel, and flash stop being separate moves and become one loud good mood
train it as a mode: one chorus per track where you commit past self-consciousness — bigger than feels reasonable, exactly as big as the music
the audit is honest: rewatch and find the moment you held back; next track, spend it

nodes.name: The boucan set — filmed
checkpoints: film one full track: groove rolling, décalé traveling, sagacité flashing, and both learned concepts dropped where the atalaku would call them
energy audit on review: is the joy visible at the end of the track, or did the face clock out early?
credit the concept sources in your journal entry — names travel with moves in this app, every style, every time

nodes.name: The floor
checkpoints: find the floor: African club nights and Ivorian diaspora parties run coupé-décalé worldwide — the atalaku will tell you what to do; do it
make thirty seconds of glorious scene — the boucan is participatory, and joining it loudly IS the etiquette
somewhere in the night, remember Abidjan's decision: the dance is proof that choosing joy is a thing a whole country can do
